name: Stepping stone
description: A flat stone set into the ground, inviting a slower path through the garden.

name: Stone path
description: Fitted paving stones that join one part of the garden to another.

name: Stone arrangement
description: A small, asymmetrical grouping of stones. Its gaps make cool hiding places.

facts.text: Odd-numbered, uneven groupings are traditional in Japanese stone arrangement.

name: Stone lantern
description: A weathered stone lantern, half-hidden by moss. It has watched over the garden for a long time.

name: Old boulder
description: A large, lichen-spotted boulder, settled deep into the ground. Frost and rain loosen small stones from it now and then.

name: Old garden gate
description: A wooden gate in the garden wall. Beyond it lies the next garden of the sanctuary.

name: Stone basin
description: A low stone water basin, the kind visitors once knelt at to rinse their hands. It still catches the rain.

facts.text: Low basins like this are called tsukubai, from a word meaning to crouch.

name: Bamboo fence
description: A low fence of bound canes that frames a planting and gives small creatures cover.

facts.text: Low bamboo fences like this traditionally edge paths and planting beds.

name: Bamboo water spout
description: A bamboo pipe that trickles water into a stone basin, with a gentle, rhythmic sound.

facts.text: Moving water brings birds down to drink and bathe.

name: Maple-leaf lantern
description: A small stone lantern dressed with red maple leaves, glowing softly at dusk.

name: Standing stone
description: A tall, weathered stone set upright in the gravel.

facts.text: Lichen grows slowly on bare stone, a few millimetres a year.

name: Raked gravel
description: Gravel raked into gentle ripples, like water.

facts.text: The ripples are raked afresh after rain.

name: Fallen log
description: An old trunk, soft with moss, slowly returning to the soil.

facts.text: Fungi slowly break the wood down into soil.

name: Log stack
description: A loose stack of deadwood, left to rot for wildlife.

facts.text: Fungi grow beside it once the wood begins to soften.

name: Little cascade
description: A tumble of stones where the stream drops and sings.

facts.text: Moving water carries fresh air into the stream.

name: Resting stone
description: A broad, flat stone set in the stream for birds to stand on.

facts.text: Wagtails stand on stones in the water, bobbing their tails.

name: Stone bench
description: A plain stone bench beneath the blossom.

facts.text: A place to sit and watch the court.

name: Petal lantern
description: A paper lantern on a post, painted with blossom.

facts.text: Its glow softens the court at dusk.

name: Boardwalk
description: A short run of timber boards over the water and mud.

facts.text: A boardwalk lets you cross the marsh without trampling it.

name: Stone bridge
description: A gentle arch of dressed stone across the water.

facts.text: Bridges in old gardens were placed to frame the best views.

name: Pavilion
description: A small open pavilion with a curved roof, for sitting by the pond.

facts.text: From here, the whole pond can be seen at once.

name: Bamboo deer-scarer
description: A bamboo arm that fills with water, tips and knocks against a stone with a hollow clack.

facts.text: Its gentle knock marks the passing of time in the garden.

name: Frog stone
description: A rounded stone with the look of a sitting frog, a lucky sign for any pond.

facts.text: Frog stones are said to bring good fortune home again.

name: Snow-viewing lantern
description: A low stone lantern with a wide roof that gathers snow beautifully.

facts.text: Its broad roof is made to hold a cap of snow in winter.

name: Mossy stump
description: An old stump softened with moss, home to beetles, woodlice and fungi.

facts.text: Rotting wood like this is a whole world for small creatures.

name: Straw bee skep
description: An old woven straw hive, kept now as a quiet corner for wild bees.

facts.text: Solitary bees nest in the hollow stems of its straw.

name: Bamboo water pipe
description: A split-bamboo pipe that carries a thin trickle of water from the stream.

facts.text: Birds come to drink and bathe at its trickle.

name: Blossom-viewing bench
description: A long low bench for sitting beneath the blossom.

facts.text: Made for the old custom of sitting to watch the blossom fall.

name: Stone bird bath
description: A shallow stone bowl of rainwater for birds to drink and bathe.

facts.text: Birds bathe to keep their feathers in good order.

name: Reed screen
description: A woven screen of reeds that shelters a quiet corner of the marsh.

facts.text: Small birds use it as a windbreak on cold days.

name: Moon-viewing platform
description: A low wooden platform for watching the moon rise over the garden.

facts.text: Moon viewing is an autumn custom, but the moon rises every season.

name: Moon gate
description: A round opening in a garden wall, framing the view beyond like a full moon.

facts.text: Stepping through a moon gate is said to bring a fresh start.
